text_fidelity_a:
Desktop Drum Set Mini Musical Instrument Rhythm Small Educational Childrens Instrument Band Novelty Toy [[VIDEOID:82c460f51abcbd27014c15e6ec79034b]] Wow. I don't want to be mean, but I want to leave an honest review too. This set is larger than I thought. I guess the measurements were buried in the description, but when I saw the basic description, I was thinking finger tapping.

This takes up about a foot of room. The drum tops are super thin plastic sheeting. Everything is, of course, some kind of plastic. The drumsticks look like Shrek's cotton swabs, made of molded gray plastic. The cymbal is silver tone and some thin metal that doesn't make much of a sound.

Now, if I wanted to encourage my child to play a musical instrumemt, I would buy them a small REAL snare drum. I would not mess with this one, even for fun.

I've been involved in music since I was 4 years old, so maybe I am pickier than some folks. But this thing is majorly annoying to hear. Like, smash it with a hammer and throw it away.
Of course, if you have someone you hate, you could give this to their kids. ;-)

IMHO, there is more value in this one to get it for decoration, and hand-paint the drums with really nice paint, and put a glitter finish on them. Then set them on a shelf to look nice.

text_fidelity_a:
Educational Insights Design & Drill All Aboard Train, 30 Piece Take Apart Toy with Electric Drill Toy, STEM Toy, Gift for Boys & Girls, Ages 3+ [[VIDEOID:979dc2c95d283020e887dc97f4539982]] There is supposed to be a motorized drill included with this set, but only the drill socket was included. Happily, the conductor has a hole on the bottom that can be used to tighten or loosen the bolts. My three-year-old niece was content with using this as is and loves the train so much as a toy that I'll give it 3 stars, but I think many children would prefer the fun of the motorized drill. When you press a button, the train makes a chu-chu sound and a very dim white light comes out the front. You can't see the light unless you're looking for it. The "design and drill" is basically some bolts to screw on to hold the covers and the wheels in place. There were several colors of bolts you can choose from to make different "designs."

The engine measures 10 inches long by 6 inches wide by 6 inches tall. The wagon measures 7.5 inches long by 6 inches wide by 3.75 inches tall. The wagon bed is 2 inches deep. The caboose measures 7.5 inches long 6 inches wide and 5 inches tall. Three AAA batteries are needed to power the drill according to the instruction manual, and two AAA batteries are needed for the train engine for the sound and light. The wheels roll smoothly and securely, and it is easy to connect the three sections of the train together, so it is a good toy not just a building activity. There are some extra bolts in case some are lost. The train is sturdy and can withstand the rough treatment of a 3-year-old armed with a plastic hammer.
text_fidelity_b: Educational Insights Design & Drill All Aboard Train, 30 Piece Take Apart Toy with Electric Drill Toy, STEM Toy, Gift for Boys & Girls, Ages 3+

Brickyard Building Blocks 177 Pieces Large Building Block Toys for Children Ages 1.5-5, Bulk Block Set, Compatible with Duplo (177 pcs) We like the Lego brand, but sometimes we need a lot of bricks without paying an exorbitant amount of money. The 1,100 piece kit from Building Bricks was exactly what we were looking for. The Big Questions:
1. Do they really work well with Lego Brand Legos?
Yes - they work very well. It's difficult to tell the difference if you're not really trying hard.
2. How much cheaper are they? Is it really worth it?
It's hard to compare exact pricing here because this set does not include wheels, doors or special pieces. If I had to choose a product to compare it to, I'd probably compare it with Lego's XXL Classic Box (https://www.amazon.com/10697-Building-Large-Creator-Pieces/dp/B00XJ5C4FW). When pricing per piece, the Lego box is about 5¢ per piece. And yes, you read that right. You're dolling out a nickel for every piece of plastic with Lego's brand stamped on it. :) Building Bricks runs about 3¢ per piece. So the answer is: It's almost half the price - very worth it if you're just needing a lot of standard pieces.
As a side note: We really liked the color choices Building Bricks made. They're perfect for expanding your Lego creation palette.

The irregularly shaped pieces, the use of colors in small areas across the entire puzzle, and the confusing curved lines in the design add greatly to the difficulty.

text_fidelity_a: 4M T-Rex Dinosaur DNA Kit, 4945, Multi What kid doesn't like dinosaurs?  This is perfert for your boy or girl who is into dinosaurs.  I suppose it could be considered an educational toy, but probably only marginally so.  Who says educational toys can't be fun too?  This is especially nice for a kid interested in archeology.  Contains a block of plaster that has embedded into it "DNA" stickers and a glow in the dark dinosaur.  After the fun of digging out the dinosaur and stickers with the included digging tools and brush, they are left with a dinosaur model, so even though the digging fun is over after one time (if they do it all at once), there is something to show for it.  There are also two "augmented reality" (AR) play mats that are completed with the DNA stickers that have been "excavated".  The mats when used with a cell phone and an application from the App Store (for Apple phones) or the Google Play Store (for Androids) produces a 3D dinosaur, visible on the phone.  One problem with this is that it might not work with all cell phones.  It is supposed to work with MOST Apple devices (8.0 and above).  On Android phones the only devices tested are Google Nexus Series, Samsung Galaxy S5 and Samsung Galaxy Tab.  I didn't have a cell phone to test this on, but it seems like it still might be fun even if that part doesn't work.  It's just that you might not be able to use the full capability of the kit if your phone doesn't work with the application.  Also if you give this to a child of only 8 (the lower age limit on this), they may not yet have a cell and you may not want them to have one at that age.  Since this contains many small parts, it needs to be kept away from small children, as there is a choking hazard (box says no one under 3).  I would have loved a toy like this when I was a kid.  Just remember to put down a newspaper when they are working on the plaster block in order to collect all the plaster pieces that are chipped off as they excavate.  Pricing of the kit is very reasonable.  Made in China.
text_fidelity_b: 4M T-Rex Dinosaur DNA Kit, 4945, Multi

4M T-Rex Dinosaur DNA Kit, 4945, Multi This is a "dig kit", which I didn't realize when I got it. My oldest has a huge obsession with dinosaurs, and they are all his brain thinks about, so I thought a dinosaur DNA kit looked like something cool for him. It's really just a dig kit, though, with some added features that require a smart phone. Honestly, we just skipped all that, and used it as a simple dig kit. Even then, we'd already did a couple of them just before this one, so the whole digging process had become a little old for him.

Aside from that, it's an okay kit. The quality of the items to dig out usually aren't great, and this was no exception. My son has had trouble getting all the pieces to stick together as they should with all the dinosaur dig kits he's ever had, and again, this one was no exception. He became a little frustrated at some of the pieces.

If you've never used a dig kit before, they're messy! We've found them to be slightly less messy done inside a pie pan. Even so, outside is always better with these things(on a warm, windless day). Also, they require patience. This one wasn't near as hard to dig through as some of the other ones we've had, but it's definitely not the easiest, either. I'd say it's a medium level on hardness. It takes time to get all the pieces, and that's part of the process. It teaches a young person a bit of what it's like for archaeologists. If they rush the dig, they end up damaging pieces.

Overall, this is a fun little lesson in patience, for both children and adults, but it wasn't quite what I was expecting.
text_fidelity_b: 4M T-Rex Dinosaur DNA Kit, 4945, Multi

Glitter Girls - Convertible Car for 14-inch Dolls - Toys, Clothes & Accessories for Girls 3-Year-Old & Up, Blue, Orange, Pink This convertible car for 14 inch dolls is completely awesome. We have a number of glitter girls dolls and two of them can fit into this convertible with ease, along with one of the glitter girls puppies sitting on a lap.

My kids saw this in a Christmas catalog and were completely enchanted with it, asking for it over and over again. It's about as big as you would expect given that the glitter girls both have to fit in there, and it has a dashboard that opens, a little side container that opens in between the two seats, two cupholders, and the trunk.

We have the glitter girls sweetshop and the accessories sweetshop that has some delightful cups of confectionery beverage, and I was delighted to find that these sweetshop beverages fit into the cupholders perfectly. (They also fit into the girls hands). The dashboard has very little room to put things in when it's open, and the angle is such that things really don't stay put very well at the dashboard is open, so I would've liked a little bit better design on that, because my kids had to work hard to find something they wanted to bring along that was small enough to fit. Same thing with the little container in between the two seats, if that could have been just a little bit wider, it would get used even more.

The trunk is also a little small and again the shape of the interior of it makes it harder for things to fit in, because it is just a rectangular box opening that is kind of slick, so when you put things in the kind of want to slide out. There is enough room in the car to where they could have made the trunk much more substantial, and it would've made this an even cooler car.

That said, these are just quibbles and the real proof of whether a toy is any good is in the pudding. My kids love it, and they've been playing with it nonstop and vrooming the girls around on all kinds of adventures since the car arrived. I've been delighted to see the amount of imaginative play that has taken place with the addition of a car, to where the girls can leave the bedroom and go on all kinds of fun adventures.

The car seems well-made and is very sturdy, the doors open, and if you need to put the windshield down for storage, it does fold down. Overall this is a great toy if you have 14 inch dolls who need some adventure in their lives.

Gamelyn Games Tiny Epic Dinosaurs,12+ years I already like Tiny Epic games. This is probably my favorite. If you can imagine a Jurassic Park game, this is more or less the one you want. Small package, great price, endless fun. What more can you ask for?

You build parks and enclosures to house dinosaurs. The dinosaurs are hungry. If you can't feed them, they'll still eat - guess what? - your other dinosaurs! Very well made and lots of fun. If you don't like this game, maybe board games aren't your thing.

I look at this game as an example to understand how to make games well. I think anyone who likes board games has to give at least one Tiny Epic game a try, and this is the one I would recommend most.

Limited closet space? Desperate for something besides Monopoly, Risk, or Settlers of Catan? Like building games with dire consequences? Think dinosaurs are the least bit cool or interesting? Look no further.

My only minor criticism is that some might consider it complex with the different special dinosaurs and some of the rules about how and when to place dinos. Any board game is going to have a learning curve, and this one is small.

At first glance, the great hall looks impressive. But the plastic is the very cheap, brittle kind. The hall has a seam down the center so two sides can swing open and shut. The first time I set this up to look at it, the "doors" would not latch shut, and then once I did get them latched, the left side got stuck and did not want to open.There are lights that flash on and off for about 5 seconds when a button is pressed. The sorting hat is attached the the wall and you can place one of the four figures under it, but it doesn't do anything else as far as I know. There is a wand YOU CAN BUY SEPARATELY that works with this playset, but I don't know what the wand can do that you cannot do manually by pushing a button or sliding a figure along. The figures included look ok, and you get Harry, Ron, Hermione, and Professor Dumbledore. No bag guy figures are included, which I feel is a missed opportunity for more play scenarios. If they threw in a Voldemort or even Snape or Draco Malfoy, there would be an antagonist other than the snake who is stuck to a tabletop and can be vanquished by flipping him upside down.
In short, I do not recommend this toy.

The Secret Life of Pets - Snowball Walking Talking Pets Figure This is a 'cute' little toy. I like the expression on his face. We've had fun playing with it for the past couple weeks.

Some things that you might want to know about it if you're considering buying one.

The instructions suggest replacing the two AAA batteries when you take the figure out of the package - the two that come in it are for 'in-store' demonstration purposes. Opening the battery compartment I found that the supplied batteries are pretty decent alkaline ones. Still, I replaced the ones in mine as I hate it when batteries go dead in a device and then leak. Something to maybe mention - the battery compartment is secured with a screw, so that small hands can't get into it.

The tail on the rabbit acts as the on/off switch. There are three setting - On, Off, and Demo. In the demonstration mode the figure talks and the wheels turn for a few seconds and then stops. When in the On position, the figure says a phrase - the wheels go for awhile and then it stops and repeats the cycle. The figure has three wheels - two fixed wheels seem to drive it's motion and a third rotates to make the figure go in different directions. Our rabbit seems to have a habit of finding the nearest corner and parking itself in it. The figure's eyes move a bit when it's in running around (although it's hard to see with the way it's eyes are set).

The figure comes with a separate carrot prop. Which the rabbit is suppose to hold in it's one hand - ours kept dropping his. So I took a piece of the white string that had secured the toy to the package and tied the carrot to his hand- you can't really even see it.

The rabbit talks, and I know it's suppose to be Kevin Hart doing a 'cartoon' voice - but it's really hard to understand what it's suppose to be saying. Hopefully when the movie comes out the phrases will be more recognizable.

All in all I like this figure and I'm looking forward to seeing the movie.
text_fidelity_b: The Secret Life of Pets - Snowball Walking Talking Pets Figure

Minsk Remote Control Stunt Car Toy, 4WD RC Cars Double Sided Rotating Vehicles 360° Flips to Bloom, 2.4GHz High Speed Rechargeable Toy Presents for 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 Year Old Boy Birthday The car itself is pretty cool. I like the way it moves its entire axels to do its stunts. You can get a pretty good idea of hwo this moves if you look at the pictures. Simple, but effective. Seems like kids younger than 8 would like this; odd because they show small kids crawling on the floor using this, but say it is for ages 8 and up. Just watch they don't try to eat the batteries, I guess. It's not super fast, either, so older kids might get bored.

Anyway, they totally cheaped out on the battery setup. 400mAh?!?! Are you kidding me? Even the cheap, "included" versions of decent brands are 1100mAh, with good ones getting 2500mAh or more. And why the goofy charging setup? You have to take it out and then hook it to an oddball USB cable (so now you can't just use any USB cable you have laying around, you have to have this one on hand). They should just wire a higher capacity battery inside and add a micro-USB port like everybody else. And maybe similar functionality for the controller, which, oddly, uses two batteries...more than the car itself.

Pretty fun. Not well thought out overall, but on the other hand, if your kids falls out of love with toys quickly, maybe it's better not to spend more for the battery setup that could have been...

Glitter Girls – Carry-On Luggage Set – Rolling Suitcase, Headphones, and Travel Essentials – 14-inch Doll Accessories – Toys for Kids Ages 3 and Up (15pcs) This, like the other Glitter Girls stuff, was purchased for book photo props and it works well for that purpose.

That said …

One complaint on one review is the ratio of the accessories’ size to the dolls’ size. I am a bit perplexed as to the complaint about the size to be honest.

As humans, our accessories are designed proportionate to our physical features and our height (in most cases); which is the same for the accessories included in this set:

Headphones
Neck pillow
Travel documents
Snacks
Eye mask
Notebook
Socks
Blanket

One I did not get was the “pen” item.

I don’t think I’d be happy with a neck pillow, eye mask, or headphones bigger than my neck, eyes, and head. It doesn’t seem practical.

All items shown are also shown in proportion to the doll, thus these are appropriately sized. Barbie items are also smaller and proportionate to the doll.

That said … this makes a great gift as a companion set to the Glitter Dolls’ line.

T.S. Shure Wooden Magnetic World Map Puzzle I cannot overstate how much I love this little magnetic world map puzzle. Geography comes alive with the little illustrations of some of the things you might find in each part of the world. The illustrations are not cartoony or tacky in any way, in fact I find them charming even as an adult.

The map comes with a wooden backing and a full set of magnet backed countries and regions. The red string on the top holds it for hanging.

The one thing I wish is that the magnets were a little stronger so that the countries would stay put a little bit better. I feel like if I have the puzzle hanging and constructed that way, the magnets work fine and do not fall unless jostled pretty good. However, I found that when I constructed it on the table and then went to hang it up, the magnets seem to want to slip. If the magnets were just a little bit stronger, it would be really fun to put the puzzle together around a table and then hang it up afterwards.

That said, the coolness of this magnetic world map can't be overstated. It is just absolutely beautiful and would make such a wonderful gift for holidays or birthdays. I am so looking forward to using this in homeschooling when my son is just a little bit older. The appealing illustrations make it such an attractive way of bringing the rest of the world to life.
text_fidelity_b: T.S. Shure Wooden Magnetic World Map Puzzle

text_fidelity_a:
Akedo Ultimate Arcade Warriors Ultimate Battle Arena Action Figure, 3 Pieces THE GOOD:
--------------
* Perfectly priced toy for the quality you're getting.
* Collectible.
* Like Rock-Em Sockem, but with electronics, and the figures will split when getting knocked out.
* This version come with an arena, but you can fight without it if you wish.
* Two warriors included to get you started.

THE BAD:
-----------
* Nothing I can think of. The price is just right for what you're getting. I don't recall an actual arcade game in the past called Akedo. It seems this toy is simply inspired by all the classic arcade fighting games such as Street Fighter, Fatal Fury, Tekken, etc. It will keep your children occupied for awhile and away from tablets.

One more thing, the two default figures that's already installed in the arena have clear bands wrapped around them. We saw the vertical bands on their bodies and cut them off. But when we battled, we still couldn't split each other. My son realize there are more tiny bands in the neck that needs to be cut. So if you're playing for awhile, and you can't knock anybody out, check to see if rubber bands are still holding their bodies tight. You can manually check... you are free of bands when you can pop their heads back and split their bodies. If you can't do that, it probably means there are some bands you still need to cut off.

text_fidelity_a: CGE Czech Games Edition Codenames Boardgame This game is best played with 4 people (two teams of two).  Your partner tries to prompt you to pick the correct cards on the table between you by giving you a single word clue and telling you how many cards on the table it relates to.  You need to decipher the hint by figuring out which of the cards they means, but don't pick the wrong one!  It could end up giving a point to the other team or if you pick the one "black card" on the table it ends the game and you instantly lose.  This game is endlessly creative and challenging as the word cards on the table and which cards correspond to your team will always be different each game.  The creative part is figuring out new ways to bundle the most cards together with a single word so you can find all your teams cards before the other team finds theirs.  It's a race to figure out the code!
